scope: Count accepted std::Write prefixes on non-Linux RawUART scalar and Mesh fallback errors. No sampling/rate/queue/airtime-policy changes. Linux runtime writer branches remain unchanged. macOS native build and physical UART validation have not been performed.
problem: write_all can accept a positive prefix before returning an error; assigning accepted only after full success leaves that physical work uncharged. Actual Linux TTYPort std::Write proof observed3584 of4100 frame bytes before TimedOut (1286ms declared35%64k air reservation).
change: Generic counted helper preserves Write::write_all Interrupted and WriteZero semantics and original errors. Both cfg(notLinux) RawUART writers retain the count through flush failure. Their existing common accounting reserves nonzero accepted bytes before returning Err, while ordinary credit and forced close remain full-success-only. Complete framing, write/flush order and clocks are unchanged.
ownership: The input frame remains borrowed and intact for same-ID retry after partial failure. No packet is logically completed by accepting its prefix.
